notes: SHIP v1.14.450 - COOLANT PLUMBING NEEDS A SOURCE (owner ruling 2026-08-12). THE DEFECT. The rear assembly was ported from the mock and drawn on EVERY rack: a CDU cartridge, two coolant manifolds and three vertical coolant pipes. Manifolds and coolant pipes are LIQUID-COOLING hardware, so drawing them on an air-cooled cabinet asserted the rack was plumbed for liquid - a fact the Master never stated. Not a small claim on this fleet: AUS-01 is H100/H200 with no Blackwell on the floor, so the plumbing was fiction on every rack there. Contract 10 and section 5, never fabricate a CDU. It was visible, too - through the empty U slots of a sparse rack the cartridge read as a green band down the middle of the FRONT elevation, which is how it was caught. THE TEST APPLIED IS THE ONE THE RAILS ALREADY PASS. The v1.14.260 rail doctrine says it plainly: the Master states totalU, so drawing totalU units of rail declares NOTHING the Master did not. Structure every cabinet physically has is honest; hardware only SOME cabinets have is a claim and needs a source. So the rear assembly is split. STRUCTURE, still unconditional: the copper bus bars (every rack is powered), the six cable-management arms, the rear door. CLAIM, now gated: the CDU cartridge, both manifolds and the three vertical pipes. THE SOURCE IS THE MASTER, NOT AN INFERENCE. A rack draws as liquid-cooled exactly when the Master places a CDU in THAT rack, read through Vocabulary.typeOf so it uses the same door the trays and the flat elevation use - and v1.14.448 giving cdu its own display key is what makes this expressible at all. Platform names are deliberately NOT consulted: this looks like a GB300 so it must be liquid is inference, and the ruling says unless the Master DECLARES it. A rack fed by a row-level CDU outside the cabinet correctly shows no in-rack plumbing, because the Master did not put one in that rack. An unreadable inventory claims nothing. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which matters because an absence-only check could be satisfied by deleting the rear assembly outright - itself a fabrication, a liquid-cooled rack drawn as if it were not plumbed. Captured side by side at iPhone width in FRONT view, the elevation where the plumbing was visible: s1:002 (H100, no CDU) now shows a clean interior with the bus bar still present, and s4:099 (CDU at RU02) keeps its cartridge and manifolds. New spec 34 asserts the gate exists, that an H100 rack resolves false and a CDU rack resolves true through Vocabulary, that the gated branch still contains the cartridge and manifold materials, and that bus bars, cable arms and the rear door stayed OUTSIDE the gate. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec ALONE): 34 = 3, 33 = 4, 32 = 3, 31 = 4, 30 = 4, 20 = 6, 15-dual-source-master = 7, 02-build-forge = 14 including the x10 aisle round trip, 08-forge-layout = 17 passed with 1 skipped. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .450. DEVICE-VERIFY: open an H100 rack and switch to FRONT. PASS is a clean rack interior with no green plumbing band showing through the empty U slots, and the copper bus bar still there. Then open s4:099, which declares a CDU at RU02 - PASS is that one still showing its plumbing. FAIL is plumbing on the H100 rack, or missing plumbing on s4:099.
